items.title: Live: Mexico ignites World Cup as three red cards rock opening game
items.description: The 2026 FIFA World Cup gets underway at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, with the opening ceremony followed by the hosts, Mexico taking on South Africa in the opening game. Follow live.

items.title: Marles 'stood up' on AUKUS trip after British minister's shock resignation
items.description: Defence Minister Richard Marles's visit to the United Kingdom has been thrown into chaos after his British counterpart John Healey resigned hours before they were due to speak.

items.title: How you and your superannuation came to be aboard SpaceX
items.description: If your superannuation is managed by any of Australia's big superannuation funds, chances are you're about to become a highly valued financial backer to Elon Musk.

items.title: Live: Trump cancels US strikes on Iran after threatening 'very hard' attack
items.description: The US president had said American forces were preparing to hit Iran "very hard". Follow live.

items.title: Air India crash plunged victims' families 'into darkness'
items.description: One year on from the fatal Air India crash that claimed 260 lives, families of victims are still waiting for a report into the investigation.

items.title: Amex ordered to compensate man whose ex accessed his data
items.description: Australia's privacy commissioner has threatened a complainant with legal action to prevent the full disclosure of the findings of a long-running investigation into American Express's information security, which found widespread technology failures.

items.title: New study not 'definitive proof' of social media harm for Australian teens
items.description: A decade-long study following almost 1,200 Melbourne school students finds a "small increased risk" of depressive symptoms for teenagers using social media at least two hours a day.

items.title: 'Broken promise' or not, Albanese's tax decision helps One Nation
items.description: There are multiple reasons why alienated voters might be generously donating to One Nation's campaign, including the prime minister's cavalier breaking of election promises that has poured kerosene on the fire under a party that can no longer be called "minor".

items.title: Couple's $3,000 wedding 'so much fun' as more Australians choose micro-events
items.description: For just $3,000, compared to the average wedding cost of about $38,000, Melbourne couple Averill and Lloyd Johnson pulled off their dream wedding.

items.title: Australians face a 'binary choice' as One Nation soars, says Chalmers
items.description: Treasurer Jim Chalmers hits out at Pauline Hanson's ties to Gina Rinehart and questions whether she actually stands for battling Australians.

items.title: Major PFAS class action could lead to multi-billion dollar claim figure
items.description: Hundreds of businesses and organisations are part of a major Victorian Supreme Court class action against chemical manufacturer 3M.

items.title: Century-old Venus flytrap mystery solved, scientists claim
items.description: Physicists think they have found the cellular mechanism behind a Venus flytrap's signature move, but plant scientists say the mystery isn't solved yet.

items.title: Falling currencies, rising inflation put pressure on international students
items.description: When Jolie Cao chose to do her undergraduate university degree in Australia, she knew it would be expensive. But an additional financial pressure has made things "really hard".

items.title: US forecasters say potentially record-breaking El Niño underway
items.description: There is a high chance this year's Pacific climate phenomenon will be among the strongest on record, which could lead to hotter temperatures across the globe.

items.title: Aboriginal people were kicked off this land. Their descendent has bought it back
items.description: Gunditjmara man Craig Molyneux buys back land that was stolen from his ancestors and infuses the property's old church with his Indigenous culture.

items.title: Friday news quiz: Fake weather, a whale graveyard and James Bond going woke
items.description: Don't let your confidence be shaken or stirred by this week's test of how much you've been paying attention.

items.title: The Cronulla riots shocked us 20 years ago. A new artwork considers their legacy
items.description: Artist Abdul Abdullah says the Cronulla riots were a "moment of revelation" for many Australians as he unveils a new work for Sydney Biennale.

items.title: Lauren can play like a 'normal kid' thanks to 600,000 strangers
items.description: Lauren Zeller has a one-in-a-million bleeding disorder, but strangers' blood donations give her a chance to play like other kids.

items.title: Man charged over Sydney woman’s alleged kidnapping murder
items.description: Family members told police they last heard from the woman on Monday, when she told them she was visiting a relative in Sydney.

items.title: Whistleblower former officer 'validated' by NSW Police culture review
items.description: Former NSW Police officers who blew the whistle on the toxic culture of the force have welcomed an independent report "validating" their experiences.

items.title: 'I don't see why you would choose this': Fears for swimming's future
items.description: Kyle Chalmers spent more than $5,000 to compete at the Australian Swimming Trials, and he says that sort of thing could drive stars away from the sport.

items.title: Celine Cremer search team member to assist with Nannup Four case
items.description: The vice-president of a search team that solved two high-profile missing persons cases in Tasmania turns his attention to the Nannup Four case after it was featured in the Expanse podcast.

items.title: Number of dogs euthanased on Sunshine Coast triples after law change
items.description: The number of dogs euthanased by a regional Queensland council has more than tripled in recent years, with more dogs put down there than in Brisbane, Australia's largest council by population size.

items.title: How One Nation could disrupt Australia's progressive stronghold
items.description: The idea that One Nation could come close to the government benches was absurd six months ago, but it is a prospect Victorian Labor MPs and insiders are increasingly discussing.

items.title: Beekeepers seek solutions as varroa mite destroys colonies
items.description: With many managed colonies under threat from the invasive varroa mite, Queensland beekeepers are trying to find ways to protect their industry.
